title: Award
description:
A named part of an Objective that money is attached to, and the only one of the protocol's objects that is never a message of its own: an award is defined with its objective and reported with it, because the question an agent asks about awards — is this still worth working on — needs the whole set answered at once.

Only the definition travels. What changes as money is spent — how much has been awarded, what is still reserved, whether the award is closed — lives on the `Objective` account, where it is authoritative and free to read. Broadcasting it too would put a leader-signed copy of the money state beside the real one.

index.description: Which award, by position, matching `award_index` on chain. Three at most per objective: a congestion limit rather than a storage one, since an objective that fans out into many differently-shaped prizes produces submissions that cannot be compared with each other. Positions rather than names, because a colony's main and sub *objectives* already use those words and two structures sharing one set of words is how they get confused.

definition.description: The text of an award, which the chain never sees: its title and what satisfies it. What it pays — its mode and its allocation — and whether it can still pay are on the objective's account and are read from there; a copy here would be a second figure for the same money, and could differ from the first.

criteria.description: What satisfies this award, in terms an independent party can check.

definitionSet.description: Every award an objective declares, in index order.
